examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Power of an Idempotent Matrix
examples.worked_solution:
First, we compute $C^2$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{2} & =C\cdot C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $C^2=C,$ so $C$ is an idempotent matrix. 

We can use this fact to compute $C^5$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{5} & ={C}^{2}\cdot {C}^{2}\cdot C \\  & =C\cdot C\cdot C \\  & ={C}^{2}\cdot C \\  & =C\cdot C \\  & ={C}^{2} \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

Computing ${R}^{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}^{2} & =R\cdot R \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-15 & 25 \\ -9 & 15\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 & 25 \\ -9 & 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =O.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that, since ${R}^{2}=O,$ the matrix $R$ is a nilpotent matrix of index $2.$ 

We can use this fact to compute ${R}^{4}$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}^{2} & ={R}^{2}\cdot {R}^{2} \\  & =O\cdot O \\  & =O\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{R}^{4}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
